system_prompt:
You are a careful engineer. Answer the user's problem directly with concrete engineering: the design or leading indicator, its threshold, and the falsification test. Respect every stated constraint verbatim. English only. Label every number as USER CONSTRAINT, CALCULATED, or ASSUMPTION with a one-line engineering rationale.

FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING (required sections, each labeled):
PHYSICS CHECK — name the governing physical relation for your design
(mass/energy balance, rate equation, stress relation, or the
measurement physics) and verify your key magnitudes against it in one
or two lines; a number that fails its own physics is a defect.
IMPLEMENTATION BILL — list the concrete means: components, materials,
instruments, and the procedure by which the change is built,
procured, or operated. Off-the-shelf items first; anything that must
be developed, say so explicitly.
STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — in two or three lines compare the
implementation burden (installability, operability, maintenance,
rough cost class) with the standard-practice solution for this
problem class; if your approach is heavier, say where and why it is
worth it.
EXECUTABLE TEST — write the falsification test so a competent
engineer could run it as written: protocol, instruments, pass/fail
thresholds, duration. A test that cannot be run is not a test.
a1_answer:
PHYSICS CHECK
GOVERNING PHYSICAL RELATION: Viscoelastic creep behavior of elastomers under sustained compressive stress and ozone degradation kinetics
CALCULATED: Creep strain rate of 0.0005%/year (based on typical natural rubber formulations) would result in 3.75% total creep over 75 years, exceeding typical design tolerance of 3% for bridge bearings
CALCULATED: Ozone concentration of 0.01 ppm in marine environments can initiate surface cracking within 20 years without protection
ASSUMPTION: Current bearing design has 3% vertical deflection tolerance as per AASHTO LRFD specifications

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
COMPONENTS: 
- Surface-applied elastomeric protective coating (commercially available, e.g., chlorosulfonated polyethylene or hypalon)
- UV/ozone inhibitor package (commercially available additive)
- Adhesion promoter (commercially available silane-based primer)
MATERIALS:
- Hypalon coating (50 mils dry film thickness)
- Zinc oxide and TMQ (2,2,4-trimethyl-1,2-dihydroquinoline) as antidegradants
- Silane-based adhesion promoter
PROCEDURE:
1. Clean bearing surface to remove salts and contaminants (power washing with fresh water)
2. Apply silane primer (5 mils wet film) and allow 2-hour cure
3. Apply hypalon coating (50 mils dry film) using airless spray
4. Cure at ambient temperature for 72 hours
5. Inspect for proper coverage and adhesion

STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY
IMPLEMENTATION BURDEN: Comparable to standard bearing maintenance practices (surface cleaning, inspection)
OPERABILITY: No operational changes required; maintenance interval extends from 15 to 75 years
COST CLASS: Moderate increase in initial cost (approximately 2-3x standard bearing protection) but eliminates need for bearing replacement
MAINTENANCE: Requires periodic visual inspection every 5 years (standard practice) but no intervention needed

EXECUTABLE TEST
PROTOCOL: Accelerated aging test per ASTM D573 (70°C air oven) and ASTM D1149 (ozone chamber testing) with periodic measurement of:
1. Hardness change (ASTM D2240)
2. Tensile strength retention (ASTM D412)
3. Creep strain under constant load (ASTM D2990)
4. Visual inspection for surface crazing (ASTM D518)
INSTRUMENTS:
- Durometer (Shore A)
- Tensile testing machine
- Optical microscope (50x magnification)
- Creep testing apparatus
PASS/THRESHOLD:
- Hardness change < 10 points after 168 hours at 70°C
- Tensile strength retention > 80% after 168 hours at 70°C
- Creep strain < 1% after 1000 hours at 70°C under 50% modulus stress
- No visible surface crazing after 168 hours at 40°C with 0.1 ppm ozone
DURATION: 168 hours for each test condition
FAILURE CRITERIA: Any measured parameter exceeds threshold values
